notes: Fixed the incompatible lead/lug joins: the motor's two wires are now 'wire-end' ports and the driver's motor output terminals M+/M- are 'header-socket' ports (the photo shows the motor's bare wires going into the module's output terminal), so the motor-to-driver joins are wire-end into header-socket and the method is 'insert'.
The wiring diagram image was not available; the circuit follows the text: driver module powered from the 3.3V pin, PWM signal from D4, plus GND, and the DC motor on the driver output.
The photo shows the driver connected via a Grove cable and a Grove-to-breadboard adapter; this is modeled as three male-to-female jumper wires from breadboard holes to the module's VCC/GND/SIG pins.
Nano Matter breadboard hole positions are assumed (the board is shown in the breadboard but exact holes are not given). Only the three used pins are modeled as inserted.
The Grove motor driver port names (VCC, GND, SIG, M+, M-) and the motor polarity are assumed.
The Google Nest Hub Max (Thread Border Router) and the Google Home app connect wirelessly over Thread/Matter, so they are not in the graph.
Power and programming come from the USB-C cable to a computer, which is not modeled.
